current_revision.mathematical_scope: Under the existing exact-tail assumptions with nonempty boundary, the metric-ball tail recovers its exponential rate and finite coefficient W(o). Triangle inclusions give |log W(o)-log W(o′)| <= h_* d(o,o′), and a finite delta-net proves uniform convergence on every compact set of basepoints in the fixed metric-measure space. Smooth Hermitian norm changes produce uniform O(exp(-T)) Hausdorff shifts of full level sets, hence preserve Busemann phases and geometric intersection masses. Formal constant depth shifts transform coordinate density coefficients, not geometric masses. The explicitly non-KE rotational cusp has tail asymptotic 2*pi*exp(ell)*R^a*exp(-R); a>0 gives a nonintegrable vanishing tensor error and no finite normalized tail coefficient, although a bounded-additive comparison with the radial ray remains. The all-right K5 cone has two distinct minimizing chords and is not CAT(0).

selected_proof_audit.author_read: Rechecked triangle inequalities and both limit orders; the finite-net uniformity bound; admissible norm changes and radial level-set Hausdorff estimates; density versus geometric mass normalization; smooth positive cap construction, exact pole distance, asymptotic tail integral and ray rough comparison; K5 angular shortest paths and cone chords.
selected_proof_audit.independent_read: The degeneration reviewer read cor:tail-intrinsic-uniform, ex:nonintegrable-cusp-tail, prop:depth-gauge and rem:K5-not-CAT0 directly and reported no gap in these specified arguments.
